subject: hep-th
title_original: Constraints on four-party entanglement in holography
authors: Vijay Balasubramanian, William K. L. Chan, Monica Jinwoo Kang, Chitraang Murdia, Simon F. Ross
abstract: We show that in pure time-reflection-symmetric holographic states all known four-party entanglement signals vanish unless the triple information $I_3$ is non-zero. In this sense, our results show that $I_3$ is the strongest known signal of the presence of quadripartite entanglement. Additionally, $I_3$ quantitatively bounds all four-party entanglement signals built from the multi-entropy. However, the residual entropy $Q_4$, also a measure of four-party entanglement, is not bounded by $I_3$, although $I_3=0$ does imply $Q_4=0$ for holographic states (except on a set of measure zero for which $Q_4$ is ill-defined).
title_relatable: What entangles four quantum systems in holographic universes?
hook: In holographic spacetimes with time symmetry, a single quantum measure—triple information—controls whether four particles can be fundamentally entangled together.
summary: In holographic states (quantum systems dual to gravity), four-party entanglement signals fail unless triple information is nonzero. The authors show triple information bounds all multi-entropy entanglement measures, making it the strongest known probe of four-particle quantum correlations. One alternative measure, residual entropy, escapes this bound but vanishes whenever triple information does.
